text:
The Canucks are now winless in nine games (0-8-1), and Thursday at Rogers Arena offered no relief. Detroit scored twice in the first nine minutes, led 5-1 early in the third, and won 5-2 behind two goals and an assist from Lucas Raymond.

Raymond opened the scoring at 4:18 of the first with a tip-in, and William Wallinder made it 2-0 less than two minutes later on a snap shot from a 3% chance. Elias Pettersson answered on the power play, but Raymond restored the lead on a Detroit man advantage with a backhand, a 78% chance by the model. Michael Rasmussen added a tip-in late in the second, and Emmitt Finnie's wrist shot early in the third made it 5-1. Jonathan Lekkerimäki scored for Vancouver in the third, but it only made the score look closer than the game was.

The play matched the result. Detroit outshot Vancouver 31-13 on goal and led in attempts 63-38. In expected goals, which measure the quality of chances taken, DET finished at 4.03 to VAN's 1.91. By the deserved-to-win measure (the share of simulated replays of every shot that a team wins), Detroit stood at 83%. Kevin Lankinen allowed about one more goal than the 31 shots against him warranted, and Vancouver's 17 giveaways to Detroit's six did not help. Detroit used three goalies' worth of shots, but Michal Postava and John Gibson each faced only a handful.

Vancouver's winless run reaches nine, with no win in the 0-8-1 stretch. The facts supplied don't include Detroit's record or streak, so all that can be said is that they took a lopsided road win.
